title: How Quickly Will Others Notice My Changes in Behavior
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece explores the substantial lag between a leader adopting a new behavior and colleagues accepting it as a genuine, lasting part of their style. It reports that while new habits can form in weeks, team members typically need six to nine months of consistent evidence before trusting the change is permanent, longer still if the behavior replaces something clearly negative, like emotional outbursts or public criticism. The author argues that leaders who change primarily to chase quick feedback-driven results rarely sustain the effort, since the proving period is simply too long to satisfy short-term expectations. It closes with a set of pointed questions testing whether a leader has the patience and internal motivation to outlast the skepticism.
points: Colleagues typically need six to nine months of consistent evidence before accepting that a leader's behavior change is genuinely permanent.
The proving period is even longer when the new behavior replaces something clearly negative, such as outbursts or public confrontation.
Leaders who change only to chase quick performance-review or feedback rewards rarely sustain the new behavior long enough to be believed.
Sustained change requires believing the new behavior reflects one's real values, independent of how quickly others notice or reward it.
quotes: Leaders don’t initially get rewarded by others for making a positive change in their leadership style.
With dedication and consistency, new habits can be created in weeks, but people won’t accept these new actions as permanent for months.
The time gap between when a leader makes a behavior change and when others accept it as a fixture of the leader’s style can be as long as six to nine months.
Leaders who make a change based only on feedback or the desire to influence others will rarely sustain the new behavior or style.
It takes a long time to convince others that you operate differently, and they won’t reward you for that change until they see the behavior dozens of times and in different situations.
